chapter_seo_title: Dao Gui Yi Xian Ch 276 – Li Huowang Exposes the Zuowandao's Ultimate Lie
chapter_meta_description: Li Huowang discovers the monstrous ghost haunting Pi County was never real—just a rumor spread by the Zuowandao. A masterclass in folk-horror debunking and mass delusion.
og_description: Li Huowang cracks the case: an entire town terrorized by a rumor. And the Zuowandao left a mahjong tile as a goodbye.
twitter_title: When the monster is just a story
twitter_description: Li Huowang proves the "shrinking ghost" was a hoax. A town's nightmare ends with an empty coffin and a mahjong tile.

lore_anchors.definition: A secret society whose name means "The Way of Sitting in Forgetfulness," a perversion of a Daoist meditative concept; they are liars and tricksters dedicated to spreading confusion and chaos for their own amusement.
A government-sponsored supernormal law enforcement body in the Dao-Twisted World; they hunt rogue cultivators and manage supernatural disasters.

A culture-bound syndrome in Chinese folk belief where individuals believe their genitals are retracting into their body; this fear is often exploited by folk healers and, in the novel, by the Zuowandao.
A mahjong tile representing the number six in the ten-thousands place; left as a taunting signature by the Zuowandao in the empty coffin.
A folk medium or ritual performer in Chinese folk religion; in this chapter, the term is used by the Zuowandao as a cover identity.

cultural_notes_faq.q: What is the "ghost that steals the root"?
cultural_notes_faq.a: In the Dao-Twisted World, it's a fabricated Zuowandao rumor that men's or women's genitals are being stolen by a ghost; in real Chinese folk belief, "suoyang" is a documented culture-bound syndrome involving fear of genital retraction.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why did Li Huowang check the magistrate's face?
cultural_notes_faq.a: He was looking for a second face underneath the skin—a telltale sign of a Zuowandao trickster, who are known to wear masks or have multiple faces.

cultural_notes_faq.q: What is the significance of the mahjong tile in the coffin?
cultural_notes_faq.a: It's a deliberate taunt left by the Zuowandao, treating the entire incident as a finished game they've won before leaving town.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why did the townspeople believe the rumor so easily?
cultural_notes_faq.a: The rumor tapped into existing folk fears (suoyang) and spread through word-of-mouth, creating mass hysteria where no one dared to question it because the "punishment" (shrinking to death) was said to come from speaking about it.

cultural_notes_faq.q: What is Li Huowang's goal here?
cultural_notes_faq.a: He's trying to join the Supervisory Heavenly Office. Solving this local crisis before an official agent arrives forces a contact and establishes his credentials.
